subject: Request: one-off onboarding credit + packaging variance for OptiMed
raw_thread:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: one-off onboarding credit + packaging variance for OptiMed

Hi Marissa / Lauren,

OptiMed (large regional healthcare provider) asked for an aggressive commercial package following our pilot:
- 35% list discount on first-year SaaS fees
- Waived onboarding professional services fee (they asked to reduce $75k to $0)
- Dedicated VPC + SOC2 evidentiary support (adds packaging and infra uplift)

Quick facts:
- ARR potential: $1.1M in year 1, with a heavy token ramp in Q1/Q2.
- Pilot over-performed (NPS + integration velocity), but procurement is pushing for credits tied to successful clinical rollout.
- They need SOC2 evidence and a private peering option — engineering estimates ~2-3 weeks extra work and a one-time infra uplift.

Attachments: financial model (20270328-optimed-mop-financials.xlsx), SOW draft (optimed-redwood-sow-draft.pdf), short exec memo (exec-memo-optimed-credit.docx).

This request is outside my approval band. I recommend elevating to VP/CFO for a one-off exception. My suggested options (ranked):
1) Approve partial onboarding credit of $50,000 + 30% first-year discount, contingent on 18-month minimum committed spend and DocuSign minimums.
2) Approve a $25,000 onboarding credit + 25% discount with a 12-month minimum and performance-based credits at 6/12 months.
3) Deny special credit; offer 20% standard discount + onboarding at 50% upfront (we keep PS fee) and add usage-based rebate schedule.

Please advise on which path you want me to present to OptiMed. If approved, I will loop legal for indemnities and include a revenue protection clause (clawback over first 12 months if usage < committed floor).

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: one-off onboarding credit + packaging variance for OptiMed

Mateo,

Thanks for the write-up — good context. A couple of quick asks before escalation:
- Can you attach a simple waterfall showing net ARR vs. gross discount impact (12/24 month view)?
- Any reference deals where we granted >30%? If so, list the revenue protections used.
- Confirm whether the VPC/infra uplift is billable as a one-time pass-through (engineering estimates) or if they expect it bundled.

My raw read: 35% + full waiver of $75k PS is steep. We should push toward option 1 with a lower onboarding credit — finance will likely want a cap. Looping Lauren for finance sign-off and Markus if VP-level commercial approval is helpful.

Thanks — Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Markus / Lauren — escalating per Marissa's note. Full context and attachments above. Short executive summary for quick review:
- Request: $75k onboarding waiver + 35% first-year discount + dedicated VPC/SOC2 support.
- Revenue: $1.1M ARR first-year potential.
- Risk: High initial usage spike, sensitive data in healthcare vertical (must meet SOC2), engineering uplift for private peering.

Recommended approval path: Approve $50k onboarding credit + 30% discount with an 18-month committed minimum and a 12-month clawback if committed minimum not met. Require DocuSign and legal signoff for revenue protection. Finance should cap the credit if revenue waterfall shows unacceptable NPV loss.

If you'd prefer a more conservative route, offer 20% + 50% onboarding fee and include a usage-based rebate tied to clinical rollout milestones.

Please reply with: APPROVE / COUNTER / DECLINE and any caps you want applied.

Thanks,
Mateo

Team,

After a quick review of the financial model Mateo attached, Finance is willing to provisionally approve a reduced onboarding credit with strict conditions. My decision framework: protect NPV, require contractual minimums, and reduce one-off exposure.

Decision (provisional): APPROVE onboarding credit of $40,000 and a 30% first-year discount, subject to all of the following being completed before signature:
- Legal signs an enforceable minimum-commitment clause (18 months) with clawback provisions for under-delivery.
- DocuSign includes a schedule tying discounts to milestone-based payments and an explicit revenue waterfall (provided by Mateo).
- Finance retains right to recoup credits if post-commitment usage falls below 70% of forecast in months 6-12.

If Legal flags the minimum as unenforceable, revert to COUNTER: 20% discount + 50% onboarding fee and a usage-rebate schedule.

Marissa — please coordinate legal. Mateo — get me the revenue waterfall and a short one-page summary of the clawback mechanics. I will sign off once the legal language is validated and the DocuSign package is ready.

Lauren Bishop
VP Finance (Acting CFO)
Redwood Inference
